questions.q: What happens to parent oleocanthal in plasma?
options: It has never been measured in human plasma; its aldehydes react with glycine and proteins
It circulates at about 25 µM for several hours
It is stored in fat tissue and released slowly
It is converted entirely into ibuprofen
questions.why: Oleocanthal disappears on contact with plasma, forming oleoglycine; in animals it is found only in the gut after oral dosing.

questions.q: How much oleocanthal does a tablespoon of high-phenolic olive oil hold compared with an ibuprofen tablet?
options: About the same as one tablet
About 0.3 to 3.4 % of a 200 to 400 mg tablet by mass
questions.why: A 13.5 g tablespoon at 100 to 500 mg/kg carries 1.35 to 6.8 mg of oleocanthal; the ibuprofen comparison describes a test-tube mechanism, not a dose.

questions.q: What does the peppery throat sting of extra virgin olive oil tell you?
options: The exact phenolic dose in mg/kg
That oleocanthal is present, through TRPA1 activation in the pharynx, not how much
That the oil has been refined
questions.why: Oleocanthal activates TRPA1, the same channel ibuprofen activates; sensitivity varies between people and food protein can abolish the sting.

questions.q: What does the only authorised EU health claim for olive oil phenolics say?
options: Olive oil reduces inflammation and pain
Olive oil protects the brain from dementia
Olive oil polyphenols contribute to the protection of blood lipids from oxidative stress
questions.why: It is a biomarker claim at 5 mg of hydroxytyrosol and derivatives per 20 g of oil, and the regulation names no measurement method.

questions.q: What phenolic content does one 13.5 g tablespoon need to deliver the claim's 5 mg?
options: About 370 mg/kg at the moment you eat it
Any extra virgin oil qualifies automatically
questions.why: 5 mg per 13.5 g is about 370 mg/kg; an oil at the 250 mg/kg threshold gives about 3.4 mg per tablespoon.

questions.q: What happened when the same 30 olive oils were analysed in five laboratories?
options: They qualified for the health claim between 1 and 21 times out of 30 depending on the protocol
None of the oils contained phenolics
Every oil qualified in every lab
questions.why: Correction factors alone moved results 2.2 to 2.5-fold, so a label number means little without its method.

questions.q: What does refining do to olive oil phenolics?
options: Removes essentially all hydroxytyrosol and tyrosol early in the process
questions.why: Refined and light olive oils keep the fatty acids and tocopherols but lose the phenolic fraction behind the health claim.

questions.q: How fast do olive oil phenolics fall during storage at room temperature?
options: They are stable for ten years
Roughly 40 to 46 % in the first year
questions.why: Losses are faster in warm storage and in oleocanthal-rich oils; cold storage at 4 °C kept about 92 % over six months.

questions.q: In what form does absorbed hydroxytyrosol mostly circulate?
options: About 98 % as conjugates, with free hydroxytyrosol near 0.03 µM after 25 mL
Bound to red blood cells for days
questions.why: The main glucuronides showed no antioxidant activity at the concentrations found in human fluids.

questions.q: Why was the 2013 PREDIMED report retracted?
options: Randomisation failures, including household co-enrolment and non-random assignment at one site
Participants were paid to report fewer events
questions.why: The 2018 republication gave almost unchanged estimates: HR 0.69 for the EVOO arm and 0.72 for nuts.

questions.q: When does olive oil lower LDL cholesterol?
options: Whenever it is added on top of the diet
Only when taken on an empty stomach
When it replaces saturated fat such as butter, lard or ghee
questions.why: Added on top of a diet it moves LDL by about +0.04 mg/dL per 10 g/day, and linoleic-rich oils lower LDL and apoB more.

questions.q: How does extra virgin olive oil behave under frying heat?
options: It forms more aldehydes than any seed oil
It is among the most oxidation-stable common oils, but heat strips 40 to 75 % of its phenolics
questions.why: EVOO outlasted seed oils before reaching the 25 % polar-compound discard limit; the cost of heat is the phenolic payload.

questions.q: What did the randomised hard-outcome trials of olive oil actually test?
options: A Mediterranean dietary package, not EVOO against refined oil or a seed oil
questions.why: PREDIMED and CORDIOPREV compared Mediterranean diets with low-fat diets or advice; no trial has compared oils on heart attacks, strokes or death.

questions.q: Which outcome carried most of PREDIMED's benefit?
options: Stroke, which fell from 24 to 14 per 1,000 over 4.8 years
questions.why: Cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.81, non-significant) and total mortality (HR 1.0) were not clearly reduced.

questions.q: What did CORDIOPREV find in coronary patients?
options: 9.6 fewer events per 1,000 person-years against a real low-fat diet, seen in men
questions.why: Events ran 28.1 against 37.7 per 1,000 person-years; two olive-oil-sector foundations co-funded the trial.

questions.q: What shape does the cohort dose-response for olive oil and mortality take?
options: A straight line with no ceiling
About 15 to 20 % lower mortality, with most of the association reached by 18 to 22 g/day
questions.why: Per 10 g/day, cardiovascular disease fell about 7 % and all-cause mortality 8 %, with the curve flattening near 20 g/day.

questions.q: In the large US cohorts, what was olive oil better than?
options: Butter, margarine, mayonnaise and dairy fat, but not other vegetable oils combined
Every other fat including seed oils
questions.why: Replacing animal or processed fats with olive oil went with 5 to 34 % lower risk; against other plant oils there was no significant difference.

questions.q: Which marker does high-phenolic olive oil lower most consistently against low-phenolic oil?
questions.why: Pools give SMD −0.25 to −0.68, the endpoint behind the EU health claim.

questions.q: How much does EVOO lower systolic blood pressure against refined olive oil?
options: About 3 mmHg over weeks, with no diastolic change
questions.why: A network meta-analysis of 13 trials found −2.87 to −2.99 mmHg at low to moderate certainty.

questions.q: Where do the headline large blood-pressure drops from olive oil come from?
options: A Cochrane review of drug trials
Trials of 23 and 24 people, while broad EVOO pools find no significant effect
questions.why: The −7.9 mmHg figure is a change from baseline, not a contrast with the polyphenol-free oil.

questions.q: How large is the phenolic effect on cholesterol?
options: HDL up 1 to 2 mg/dL; LDL down 4 to 5 mg/dL only at high phenolic doses
LDL down by half, like a statin
questions.why: EUROLIVE's phenolic HDL increment was about 0.8 mg/dL between the low and high oils.

questions.q: What did the EVOO-only meta-analysis of 33 trials find for inflammatory markers?
options: No effect on CRP, IL-6, IL-10 or TNF-α
questions.why: Reductions appear when olive oil comes inside a Mediterranean diet, not when EVOO is tested alone.

questions.q: What is the most reproducible human effect of oleocanthal-rich oil?
options: Lower blood glucose within an hour
Acute dampening of ex vivo platelet aggregation after 40 mL
questions.why: Two small trials of 9 and 10 people found the effect; the first trial's authors concluded it did not run through COX.

questions.q: What do olive oil interventions do to HbA1c in type 2 diabetes?
options: Lower it by about 0.27 percentage points
questions.why: Fasting glucose fell 0.44 mmol/L across 29 trials; PREDIMED's diabetes result is a secondary subgroup analysis.

questions.q: How much phenolic content does a typical premium EVOO hold?
options: About 340 to 420 mg/kg by LC-MS/MS, with one in six to one in four below the claim threshold
questions.why: Greek qNMR samples averaged 483 mg/kg; oleocanthal alone ranged from non-detectable to 355 mg/kg across 175 oils.

questions.q: What did screens of retail extra virgin olive oil find?
options: Every bottle is pure seed oil
A large share fails some grade criterion, mostly refined-oil admixture or sensory defects, with rates depending on the method
Only olive oil from Greece is ever adulterated
questions.why: An FDA screen flagged 62.5 % of 88 products, while fatty-acid limits alone would flag fewer than 10 %.

questions.q: Did the HDL efflux improvement from high-phenolic oil replicate?
options: No: it appeared in one EUROLIVE sub-study and not in OLIVAUS at more than twice the dose
questions.why: PREDIMED's efflux gain was against baseline, not against the control diet.

questions.q: How should the EVOO-only PREDIMED signals for atrial fibrillation, diabetes and breast cancer be read?
options: As effects seen equally in the nut arm
As post hoc or secondary analyses with few events, corrected but not retracted
questions.why: The breast cancer result rests on 35 cases; the nut arm was null on each outcome.

questions.q: What do Spanish cohorts suggest about virgin versus common olive oil?
options: Virgin oil tracks lower mortality while common oil does not, but no trial has compared grades
There is no difference at all
questions.why: Virgin oil carried all-cause HR 0.66 against 0.96 for common oil in a Spanish national sample.

questions.q: What happens to blood vessel function after a large olive oil fat load eaten alone?
options: It can blunt flow-mediated dilation for hours, while high-phenolic oil or oil with vegetables does not
questions.why: A 50 g fat load cut FMD by 31 %; 50 mL of high-polyphenol EVOO against refined oil gave a 4.8-point FMD advantage.

questions.q: How does olive oil's effect on flow-mediated dilation compare with other foods?
options: Ten times larger than any other food
About +0.8 points, similar to tea, cocoa, soy, nuts and vegetables
questions.why: Mediterranean diets give +1.66 to +2.32 points; tea gave +3.22 in the same large meta-analysis.

questions.q: Where does the oleocanthal amyloid-clearance mechanism come from?
options: Mouse studies by one commercially linked laboratory network, with no human measurement
questions.why: The key experiments injected pure oleocanthal; investigators declare roles in a company developing oleocanthal products.

questions.q: What happened in the 26-person US trial of high-phenolic EVOO in mild cognitive impairment?
options: Refined olive oil improved the dementia rating at least as much as EVOO
questions.why: The overall blood-brain barrier permeability change was not significant, and the oil was donated by its producer.

questions.q: What can the cohort link between olive oil and dementia-related death not do?
options: Separate oil grades, and it vanishes when olive oil is compared with other vegetable oils
questions.why: Half a tablespoon a day carried HR 0.72 for dementia-related death, which is not the same as dementia incidence.

questions.q: Is there a randomised trial showing extra virgin olive oil relieves pain?
options: Yes, it matches ibuprofen for headaches
No, none exists; the closest evidence is olive extracts in osteoarthritis
Yes, but only for back pain
questions.why: Olive extracts pool to a modest, uncertain effect from three trials, and an olive-leaf trial was null on its primary outcome.

questions.q: What did the MIND trial find, in which the diet arm received about two tablespoons of EVOO a day for three years?
options: No cognitive or MRI benefit compared with the control
questions.why: Global cognition improved +0.205 against +0.170 in controls (P = 0.23).

questions.q: Which statement about PREDIMED is accurate?
options: Its retraction did not collapse the evidence, and it never proved EVOO itself prevents heart attacks
It proved olive oil prevents all heart attacks
Its retraction showed the diet had no effect
It tested olive oil against seed oils
questions.why: The republished estimates barely moved, while heart attacks and cardiovascular death were not clearly reduced and nuts did as well.

questions.q: What does an oil's smoke point mainly track?
options: Free acidity, so it is a poor guide to oxidation products
questions.why: EVOO formed fewer polar compounds and aldehydes than seed oils in frying tests, and oil type did not change acrylamide.

questions.q: Does genetic evidence show that oleic acid itself protects against heart attack?
options: No: genetically higher oleic acid was not associated with heart disease or stroke
It shows oleic acid causes heart attacks
questions.why: Stroke associations in another genetic study were driven by a pleiotropic desaturase locus.

questions.q: Is there human evidence that EVOO lowers blood pressure through nitro-oleic acid?
options: Yes, from a large human trial
Yes, it is the main mechanism
No: the evidence is mouse and test-tube work
questions.why: The mouse study injected nitro-oleic acid, and in humans adding a fat to nitrite blunted its vessel-widening effect.

questions.q: Which features best predict what phenolics actually reach your spoon?
options: Recent harvest date, a phenolic value with its method and date, and opaque packaging
A green glass bottle and a high price
The words extra virgin on the label
A dark colour of the oil
questions.why: Phenolics fall 40 to 46 % a year, methods differ two- to threefold, and tin or bag-in-box beat green glass and PET.

questions.q: How should a daily tablespoon of EVOO be used to get the most from it?
options: Heated to its smoke point first
Raw, replacing butter, margarine or mayonnaise rather than added on top
Added on top of all other fats
questions.why: A 170 °C sauté removes about 75 % of phenolics, and the cholesterol and cohort benefits come from what the oil replaces.

questions.q: What is the better way to raise your phenolic dose without adding calories?
options: Drink a glass of oil daily
Heat the oil to concentrate it
Choose a higher-phenolic oil rather than pouring more
questions.why: 8 g of a 1,021 mg/kg oil delivered the same phenolic dose as 20 g of a 414 mg/kg oil.

questions.q: What does the evidence say about taking olive oil as a fasted morning shot?
options: It is required for any benefit
No trial favours it over taking oil with food, and a fasted bolus contracts the gallbladder
questions.why: A 50 mL EVOO bolus is used clinically to test gallbladder contraction; the flush claim rests on one uncontrolled case.

questions.q: Which safety statement about food-dose olive oil is supported?
options: No documented allergy to the oil, no warfarin interaction study, and contaminants concentrated in pomace oil
It interacts dangerously with warfarin at any dose
Extra virgin oil carries the most PAH contamination
questions.why: A measurable platelet effect at 40 mL is a reason to mention a very high-oleocanthal oil to a prescriber if you take antiplatelet drugs or anticoagulants.
